The **2010 [NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament")** involved 65 teams playing in a single-elimination tournament that determined the National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) Division I men's basketball national champion for the [2009–10 basketball season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_season "2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season"). The 72nd annual edition of the tournament began on March 16, 2010, and concluded with the [championship game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Championship_Game "2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game") on April 5, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Indiana.

The Final Four consisted of [Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Duke_Blue_Devils_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team"), making their first appearance since [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2004 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_West_Virginia_Mountaineers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team"), who were making their second appearance and first since 1959, [Butler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Butler_Bulldogs_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team"), considered the host school and making their first ever appearance, and [Michigan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Michigan_State_Spartans_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team"), the national runner-up from [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament") appearing in the Final Four for the sixth time under head coach Tom Izzo.

When Duke and Butler played each other in the tournament final, it was the first title game between private universities in 25 years ([Villanova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984%E2%80%9385_Villanova_Wildcats_men's_basketball_team "1984–85 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team") and [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984%E2%80%9385_Georgetown_Hoyas_men's_basketball_team "1984–85 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team") met in [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1985 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament")), and the fifth such match-up in history (1942, 1954, and 1955 having been the other years). Duke defeated Butler 61–59 in the championship game as Gordon Hayward's last second desperation shot clanged off the rim. It was Duke's first national championship since [2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2001 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament") and fourth overall.

Entering the tournament, the top four seeds were [Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kansas_Jayhawks_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team"), Duke, [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kentucky_Wildcats_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team"), and [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Syracuse_Orange_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team"). Kansas entered the Tournament as the overall No. 1 seed but was defeated in the opening weekend by [Northern Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Northern_Iowa_Panthers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball team"), the No. 9 seed in the Midwest region. Northern Iowa was one of four teams seeded lower than No. 8 to advance to the Sweet Sixteen, joining the East Region's No. 11 seed [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Washington_Huskies_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Washington Huskies men's basketball team"), No. 12 seed [Cornell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Cornell_Big_Red_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Cornell Big Red men's basketball team") and the South Region's No. 10 seed [Saint Mary's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Saint_Mary's_Gaels_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball team").

## Schedule and venues
### Final Four - Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis, Indiana
The biggest upset of the first day came in Providence, Rhode Island, where 14th-seeded [Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Ohio_Bobcats_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team") defeated third-seeded [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Georgetown_Hoyas_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team") in convincing fashion, 97–83, for their first Tournament win since [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1983 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), when they ousted [Illinois State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_State_Redbirds_men's_basketball "Illinois State Redbirds men's basketball") in the first round of that Tournament. Armon Bassett scored 32 points for the Bobcats, who shot 57 percent from the field and made 13 of 23 3-pointers.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-6) They advanced to face Tennessee, the sixth seed in the region. The Volunteers held off 11th seed [San Diego State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_San_Diego_State_Aztecs_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team"), 62–59, on head coach Bruce Pearl's 50th birthday. ## Schedule and venues
### Final Four - Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis, Indiana
Prince and Melvin Goins scored 15 points each for Tennessee.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-7)
In Oklahoma City, Ali Farokhmanesh drilled a three-pointer with 4.9 seconds remaining to lift ninth-seeded [Northern Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Northern_Iowa_Panthers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball team") over [UNLV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UNLV_Runnin'_Rebels_basketball_team "2009–10 UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball team"). It was the Panthers first Tournament win since [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1990 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-8) UNI advanced to face top-seeded [Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kansas_Jayhawks_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team"). The top seed withheld an effort by [Lehigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehigh_Mountain_Hawks_men's_basketball "Lehigh Mountain Hawks men's basketball"), trailing the 16th seed early in the game and leading by just six at halftime before pulling away midway in the second half for a 90–74 win.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-9)

## Schedule and venues
### Final Four - Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis, Indiana
On the second day of play, 10th-seeded [Georgia Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Georgia_Tech_Yellow_Jackets_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team") failed to make a single field goal in the final 8:19 of play, but sank 13 free throws to hold off No. 7 Oklahoma State, 64–59, in Milwaukee. Gani Lawal led Georgia Tech with 14 points.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-10) The Yellow Jackets advanced to play [Ohio State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Ohio_State_Buckeyes_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team"), who defeated [UC Santa Barbara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UC_Santa_Barbara_Gauchos_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball team") 68–51. Buckeye star Evan Turner struggled from the field, shooting 2–13 and scoring nine points, and the Gauchos put up a fight, playing from behind most of the game.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-11)

## Schedule and venues
### Final Four - Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis, Indiana
Rounding out the Midwest bracket were [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Maryland_Terrapins_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team") and [Michigan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Michigan_State_Spartans_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team") in Spokane, Washington. The Terrapins beat [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Cougars_men's_basketball "Houston Cougars men's basketball") 89–77 behind a career-high 21 points and 17 rebounds from freshman Jordan Williams,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-12) while the Spartans edged [New Mexico State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_New_Mexico_State_Aggies_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball team"), 70–67. The end of the game included a controversial lane violation call on Aggies player Troy Gillenwater with 18.6 seconds left that allowed MSU to reshoot a missed free throw and extend its lead to 3.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-13)

texts.1: The **2010 [NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament")** involved 65 teams playing in a single-elimination tournament that determined the National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) Division I men's basketball national champion for the [2009–10 basketball season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_season "2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season"). The 72nd annual edition of the tournament began on March 16, 2010, and concluded with the [championship game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Championship_Game "2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game") on April 5, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Indiana.
texts.2: The Final Four consisted of [Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Duke_Blue_Devils_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team"), making their first appearance since [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2004 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_West_Virginia_Mountaineers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team"), who were making their second appearance and first since 1959, [Butler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Butler_Bulldogs_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team"), considered the host school and making their first ever appearance, and [Michigan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Michigan_State_Spartans_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team"), the national runner-up from [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament") appearing in the Final Four for the sixth time under head coach Tom Izzo.
texts.3: When Duke and Butler played each other in the tournament final, it was the first title game between private universities in 25 years ([Villanova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984%E2%80%9385_Villanova_Wildcats_men's_basketball_team "1984–85 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team") and [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984%E2%80%9385_Georgetown_Hoyas_men's_basketball_team "1984–85 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team") met in [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1985 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament")), and the fifth such match-up in history (1942, 1954, and 1955 having been the other years). Duke defeated Butler 61–59 in the championship game as Gordon Hayward's last second desperation shot clanged off the rim. It was Duke's first national championship since [2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2001 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament") and fourth overall.
texts.4: Entering the tournament, the top four seeds were [Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kansas_Jayhawks_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team"), Duke, [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kentucky_Wildcats_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team"), and [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Syracuse_Orange_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team"). Kansas entered the Tournament as the overall No. 1 seed but was defeated in the opening weekend by [Northern Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Northern_Iowa_Panthers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball team"), the No. 9 seed in the Midwest region. Northern Iowa was one of four teams seeded lower than No. 8 to advance to the Sweet Sixteen, joining the East Region's No. 11 seed [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Washington_Huskies_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Washington Huskies men's basketball team"), No. 12 seed [Cornell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Cornell_Big_Red_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Cornell Big Red men's basketball team") and the South Region's No. 10 seed [Saint Mary's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Saint_Mary's_Gaels_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball team").

## Schedule and venues
### Final Four - Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis, Indiana
The biggest upset of the first day came in Providence, Rhode Island, where 14th-seeded [Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Ohio_Bobcats_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team") defeated third-seeded [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Georgetown_Hoyas_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team") in convincing fashion, 97–83, for their first Tournament win since [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1983 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), when they ousted [Illinois State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_State_Redbirds_men's_basketball "Illinois State Redbirds men's basketball") in the first round of that Tournament. Armon Bassett scored 32 points for the Bobcats, who shot 57 percent from the field and made 13 of 23 3-pointers.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-6) They advanced to face Tennessee, the sixth seed in the region. The Volunteers held off 11th seed [San Diego State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_San_Diego_State_Aztecs_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team"), 62–59, on head coach Bruce Pearl's 50th birthday. ## Schedule and venues
### Final Four - Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis, Indiana
Prince and Melvin Goins scored 15 points each for Tennessee.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-7)
In Oklahoma City, Ali Farokhmanesh drilled a three-pointer with 4.9 seconds remaining to lift ninth-seeded [Northern Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Northern_Iowa_Panthers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball team") over [UNLV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UNLV_Runnin'_Rebels_basketball_team "2009–10 UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball team"). It was the Panthers first Tournament win since [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1990 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-8) UNI advanced to face top-seeded [Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kansas_Jayhawks_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team"). The top seed withheld an effort by [Lehigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehigh_Mountain_Hawks_men's_basketball "Lehigh Mountain Hawks men's basketball"), trailing the 16th seed early in the game and leading by just six at halftime before pulling away midway in the second half for a 90–74 win.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-9)

## Schedule and venues
### Final Four - Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis, Indiana
On the second day of play, 10th-seeded [Georgia Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Georgia_Tech_Yellow_Jackets_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team") failed to make a single field goal in the final 8:19 of play, but sank 13 free throws to hold off No. 7 Oklahoma State, 64–59, in Milwaukee. Gani Lawal led Georgia Tech with 14 points.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-10) The Yellow Jackets advanced to play [Ohio State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Ohio_State_Buckeyes_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team"), who defeated [UC Santa Barbara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UC_Santa_Barbara_Gauchos_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball team") 68–51. Buckeye star Evan Turner struggled from the field, shooting 2–13 and scoring nine points, and the Gauchos put up a fight, playing from behind most of the game.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-11)

## Schedule and venues
### Final Four - Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis, Indiana
Rounding out the Midwest bracket were [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Maryland_Terrapins_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team") and [Michigan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Michigan_State_Spartans_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team") in Spokane, Washington. The Terrapins beat [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Cougars_men's_basketball "Houston Cougars men's basketball") 89–77 behind a career-high 21 points and 17 rebounds from freshman Jordan Williams,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-12) while the Spartans edged [New Mexico State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_New_Mexico_State_Aggies_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball team"), 70–67. The end of the game included a controversial lane violation call on Aggies player Troy Gillenwater with 18.6 seconds left that allowed MSU to reshoot a missed free throw and extend its lead to 3.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-13)

The **2010 [NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament")** involved 65 teams playing in a single-elimination tournament that determined the National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) Division I men's basketball national champion for the [2009–10 basketball season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_season "2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season"). The 72nd annual edition of the tournament began on March 16, 2010, and concluded with the [championship game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Men's_Division_I_Basketball_Championship_Game "2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game") on April 5, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Indiana.

The Final Four consisted of [Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Duke_Blue_Devils_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team"), making their first appearance since [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2004 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_West_Virginia_Mountaineers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team"), who were making their second appearance and first since 1959, [Butler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Butler_Bulldogs_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team"), considered the host school and making their first ever appearance, and [Michigan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Michigan_State_Spartans_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team"), the national runner-up from [2009](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament") appearing in the Final Four for the sixth time under head coach Tom Izzo.

When Duke and Butler played each other in the tournament final, it was the first title game between private universities in 25 years ([Villanova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984%E2%80%9385_Villanova_Wildcats_men's_basketball_team "1984–85 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team") and [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984%E2%80%9385_Georgetown_Hoyas_men's_basketball_team "1984–85 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team") met in [1985](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1985_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1985 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament")), and the fifth such match-up in history (1942, 1954, and 1955 having been the other years). Duke defeated Butler 61–59 in the championship game as Gordon Hayward's last second desperation shot clanged off the rim. It was Duke's first national championship since [2001](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "2001 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament") and fourth overall.

Entering the tournament, the top four seeds were [Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kansas_Jayhawks_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team"), Duke, [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kentucky_Wildcats_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team"), and [Syracuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Syracuse_Orange_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team"). Kansas entered the Tournament as the overall No. 1 seed but was defeated in the opening weekend by [Northern Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Northern_Iowa_Panthers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball team"), the No. 9 seed in the Midwest region. Northern Iowa was one of four teams seeded lower than No. 8 to advance to the Sweet Sixteen, joining the East Region's No. 11 seed [Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Washington_Huskies_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Washington Huskies men's basketball team"), No. 12 seed [Cornell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Cornell_Big_Red_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Cornell Big Red men's basketball team") and the South Region's No. 10 seed [Saint Mary's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Saint_Mary's_Gaels_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Saint Mary's Gaels men's basketball team").

## Schedule and venues
### Final Four - Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis, Indiana
The biggest upset of the first day came in Providence, Rhode Island, where 14th-seeded [Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Ohio_Bobcats_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Ohio Bobcats men's basketball team") defeated third-seeded [Georgetown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Georgetown_Hoyas_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team") in convincing fashion, 97–83, for their first Tournament win since [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1983 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament"), when they ousted [Illinois State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_State_Redbirds_men's_basketball "Illinois State Redbirds men's basketball") in the first round of that Tournament. Armon Bassett scored 32 points for the Bobcats, who shot 57 percent from the field and made 13 of 23 3-pointers.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-6) They advanced to face Tennessee, the sixth seed in the region. The Volunteers held off 11th seed [San Diego State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_San_Diego_State_Aztecs_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team"), 62–59, on head coach Bruce Pearl's 50th birthday. J. P.

## Schedule and venues
### Final Four - Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis, Indiana
Prince and Melvin Goins scored 15 points each for Tennessee.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-7)
In Oklahoma City, Ali Farokhmanesh drilled a three-pointer with 4.9 seconds remaining to lift ninth-seeded [Northern Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Northern_Iowa_Panthers_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball team") over [UNLV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UNLV_Runnin'_Rebels_basketball_team "2009–10 UNLV Runnin' Rebels basketball team"). It was the Panthers first Tournament win since [1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament "1990 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-8) UNI advanced to face top-seeded [Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Kansas_Jayhawks_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team"). The top seed withheld an effort by [Lehigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lehigh_Mountain_Hawks_men's_basketball "Lehigh Mountain Hawks men's basketball"), trailing the 16th seed early in the game and leading by just six at halftime before pulling away midway in the second half for a 90–74 win.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-9)

## Schedule and venues
### Final Four - Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis, Indiana
On the second day of play, 10th-seeded [Georgia Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Georgia_Tech_Yellow_Jackets_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball team") failed to make a single field goal in the final 8:19 of play, but sank 13 free throws to hold off No. 7 Oklahoma State, 64–59, in Milwaukee. Gani Lawal led Georgia Tech with 14 points.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-10) The Yellow Jackets advanced to play [Ohio State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Ohio_State_Buckeyes_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team"), who defeated [UC Santa Barbara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_UC_Santa_Barbara_Gauchos_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 UC Santa Barbara Gauchos men's basketball team") 68–51. Buckeye star Evan Turner struggled from the field, shooting 2–13 and scoring nine points, and the Gauchos put up a fight, playing from behind most of the game.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-11)

## Schedule and venues
### Final Four - Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis, Indiana
Rounding out the Midwest bracket were [Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Maryland_Terrapins_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team") and [Michigan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Michigan_State_Spartans_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team") in Spokane, Washington. The Terrapins beat [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Cougars_men's_basketball "Houston Cougars men's basketball") 89–77 behind a career-high 21 points and 17 rebounds from freshman Jordan Williams,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-12) while the Spartans edged [New Mexico State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_New_Mexico_State_Aggies_men's_basketball_team "2009–10 New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball team"), 70–67. The end of the game included a controversial lane violation call on Aggies player Troy Gillenwater with 18.6 seconds left that allowed MSU to reshoot a missed free throw and extend its lead to 3.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_NCAA_Division_I_men's_basketball_tournament#cite_note-13)

# Butler, Ebanks Drafted
Butler, Ebanks Drafted
June 25, 2010 09:47 AM  | General
Share:
By John Antonik for MSNsportsNET.com
June 25, 2010
**Devin Ebanks**
MORGANTOWN, W.Va. – Da’Sean Butler and Devin Ebanks were selected in Thursday night’s NBA draft held in New York City. Butler was the 42nd selection in the second round by the Miami Heat while Ebanks was taken one pick later by the defending world champion Los Angeles Lakers.
“I’m so happy right now, you don’t understand,” Ebanks said. “The world champions … I get to play with the best player in the world, Kobe Bryant … I don’t really have too many words to say. I’m just happy.”
Butler is also pleased.
When he injured his knee midway through the second half of West Virginia’s Final Four game against Duke there were doubts that Butler would even get drafted despite once being projected as a first-round choice.
Butler worked hard to rehabilitate his knee and the Heat thought enough of his potential to make the call.
“I was literally just overwhelmed,” said Butler. "I started to cry for a second.”
Butler was one of three players selected by Miami in the second round joining Texas center Dexter Pittman and Mississippi State forward Jarvis Varnado. Last year Miami had a 47-35 record and finished third in the Southeast Division before losing in the first round of the playoffs to Boston.
Ebanks was one of two players taken by the Lakers; Texas El-Paso forward Derrick Caracter was taken 58th.
Ebanks averaged 12 points and 8.1 rebounds per game in helping the Mountaineers to their first Final Four appearance in 51 years.
**Da'Sean Butler**
Butler averaged 17.2 points per game and became only the third player in school history to score 2,000 career points. The other two were Hot Rod Hundley and Jerry West.

# Butler, Ebanks Drafted
“I feel good, I mean you hear so much, ‘he doesn’t do this, he doesn’t do that,’ ” Butler said. “I mean I have a lot more work and a lot more things to accomplish to prove everybody wrong about me so I’m just looking forward to the season, that’s about it.”
West Virginia made the NCAA tournament during three of Butler’s four seasons playing for the Mountaineers and the other year they won the NIT when he was a freshman.
“It’s been a long, long journey,” Butler said.
The selections of Butler and Ebanks marks the first time in school history West Virginia has had two players taken since the draft was paired to only two rounds. The last time two Mountaineer players went in the draft was 1983 when guard Greg Jones was selected in the third round by the Indiana Pacers and forward Russel Todd was drafted in the sixth round by the Milwaukee Bucks.
It also represents the second and third Bob Huggins-coached players taken in the draft since Huggins has been at WVU; Huggins has had 18 players drafted during his coaching career.
“I’m willing to learn,” Ebanks said. “They just won the NBA championship, so I have a whole bunch of stuff to learn about the NBA and what better team than the Lakers?”

# Butler, Ebanks Drafted
Butler, Ebanks Drafted
June 25, 2010 09:47 AM  | General
Share:
By John Antonik for MSNsportsNET.com
June 25, 2010
**Devin Ebanks**
MORGANTOWN, W.Va. – Da’Sean Butler and Devin Ebanks were selected in Thursday night’s NBA draft held in New York City. Butler was the 42nd selection in the second round by the Miami Heat while Ebanks was taken one pick later by the defending world champion Los Angeles Lakers.
“I’m so happy right now, you don’t understand,” Ebanks said. “The world champions … I get to play with the best player in the world, Kobe Bryant … I don’t really have too many words to say. I’m just happy.”
Butler is also pleased.
When he injured his knee midway through the second half of West Virginia’s Final Four game against Duke there were doubts that Butler would even get drafted despite once being projected as a first-round choice.
Butler worked hard to rehabilitate his knee and the Heat thought enough of his potential to make the call.
“I was literally just overwhelmed,” said Butler. "I started to cry for a second.”
Butler was one of three players selected by Miami in the second round joining Texas center Dexter Pittman and Mississippi State forward Jarvis Varnado. Last year Miami had a 47-35 record and finished third in the Southeast Division before losing in the first round of the playoffs to Boston.
Ebanks was one of two players taken by the Lakers; Texas El-Paso forward Derrick Caracter was taken 58th.
Ebanks averaged 12 points and 8.1 rebounds per game in helping the Mountaineers to their first Final Four appearance in 51 years.
**Da'Sean Butler**
Butler averaged 17.2 points per game and became only the third player in school history to score 2,000 career points. The other two were Hot Rod Hundley and Jerry West.

# Butler, Ebanks Drafted
“I feel good, I mean you hear so much, ‘he doesn’t do this, he doesn’t do that,’ ” Butler said. “I mean I have a lot more work and a lot more things to accomplish to prove everybody wrong about me so I’m just looking forward to the season, that’s about it.”
West Virginia made the NCAA tournament during three of Butler’s four seasons playing for the Mountaineers and the other year they won the NIT when he was a freshman.
“It’s been a long, long journey,” Butler said.
The selections of Butler and Ebanks marks the first time in school history West Virginia has had two players taken since the draft was paired to only two rounds. The last time two Mountaineer players went in the draft was 1983 when guard Greg Jones was selected in the third round by the Indiana Pacers and forward Russel Todd was drafted in the sixth round by the Milwaukee Bucks.
It also represents the second and third Bob Huggins-coached players taken in the draft since Huggins has been at WVU; Huggins has had 18 players drafted during his coaching career.
“I’m willing to learn,” Ebanks said. “They just won the NBA championship, so I have a whole bunch of stuff to learn about the NBA and what better team than the Lakers?”

# Butler, Ebanks Drafted
Butler, Ebanks Drafted
June 25, 2010 09:47 AM  | General
Share:
By John Antonik for MSNsportsNET.com
June 25, 2010
**Devin Ebanks**
MORGANTOWN, W.Va. – Da’Sean Butler and Devin Ebanks were selected in Thursday night’s NBA draft held in New York City. Butler was the 42nd selection in the second round by the Miami Heat while Ebanks was taken one pick later by the defending world champion Los Angeles Lakers.
“I’m so happy right now, you don’t understand,” Ebanks said. “The world champions … I get to play with the best player in the world, Kobe Bryant … I don’t really have too many words to say. I’m just happy.”
Butler is also pleased.
When he injured his knee midway through the second half of West Virginia’s Final Four game against Duke there were doubts that Butler would even get drafted despite once being projected as a first-round choice.
Butler worked hard to rehabilitate his knee and the Heat thought enough of his potential to make the call.
“I was literally just overwhelmed,” said Butler. "I started to cry for a second.”
Butler was one of three players selected by Miami in the second round joining Texas center Dexter Pittman and Mississippi State forward Jarvis Varnado. Last year Miami had a 47-35 record and finished third in the Southeast Division before losing in the first round of the playoffs to Boston.
Ebanks was one of two players taken by the Lakers; Texas El-Paso forward Derrick Caracter was taken 58th.
Ebanks averaged 12 points and 8.1 rebounds per game in helping the Mountaineers to their first Final Four appearance in 51 years.
**Da'Sean Butler**
Butler averaged 17.2 points per game and became only the third player in school history to score 2,000 career points. The other two were Hot Rod Hundley and Jerry West.

“I feel good, I mean you hear so much, ‘he doesn’t do this, he doesn’t do that,’ ” Butler said. “I mean I have a lot more work and a lot more things to accomplish to prove everybody wrong about me so I’m just looking forward to the season, that’s about it.”
West Virginia made the NCAA tournament during three of Butler’s four seasons playing for the Mountaineers and the other year they won the NIT when he was a freshman.
“It’s been a long, long journey,” Butler said.
The selections of Butler and Ebanks marks the first time in school history West Virginia has had two players taken since the draft was paired to only two rounds. The last time two Mountaineer players went in the draft was 1983 when guard Greg Jones was selected in the third round by the Indiana Pacers and forward Russel Todd was drafted in the sixth round by the Milwaukee Bucks.
It also represents the second and third Bob Huggins-coached players taken in the draft since Huggins has been at WVU; Huggins has had 18 players drafted during his coaching career.
“I’m willing to learn,” Ebanks said. “They just won the NBA championship, so I have a whole bunch of stuff to learn about the NBA and what better team than the Lakers?”
